title: Working shown, or working used?
allegory: Chain-of-thought faithfulness is like checking a student's neat working: it counts as their real reasoning only if changing a line would change their answer, and only if nothing they left unwritten, like a whispered hint, decided it.
map: a friend's whisper the working never mentions
a cue in the prompt that sways the answer but is never verbalised
rewrite one line and see if the answer changes
a counterfactual or resampling test: how far the answer distribution moves

chapters.name: Neat working
chapters.note: it reads so well... but is it why?

props.label: step 1 ... step 2 ... step 3 ... so the answer is B

cap.1: A model writes out its reasoning step by step, then answers. It reads beautifully. But is that written reasoning actually why it gave that answer?
cap.2: Chain of thought gives you readable text before the answer, and it's tempting to treat it as a transcript of the computation. Faithfulness asks whether it is.
cap.3: CoT faithfulness: whether the verbalised reasoning reflects the causal process behind the output. Fluency and correctness of the text don't establish that.

props.label: neat working, no mention of any whisper

cap.1: Think of a student's neat working. If a friend whispered the answer, the working might never mention it. It looks like reasoning; the whisper did the work.
cap.2: The CoT is the working; the answer is what gets graded. A cue in the prompt can steer the answer while the reasoning never mentions it: readable, but not the real cause.
cap.3: Two ways stated and used reasoning can come apart: omission (a causal factor goes unverbalised) and post-hoc rationalisation (text generated to justify an answer reached another way).

parts.note: answer odds with line i as written
with line i swapped for another

cap.1: To check, change one line of the working and see whether the answer changes. If rewriting a step never moves the answer, that step wasn't doing the work.
cap.2: Swap sentence i for an alternative, regenerate, and measure how much the answer distribution moves. A big Δ means the sentence was load-bearing; near zero means decorative.
cap.3: Faithfulness becomes a causal question: intervene on the CoT (replace, resample or truncate sentences) and measure the shift in the answer distribution.

cap.1: Another poke: stop the working halfway and ask for the answer. If the answer was settled before the reasoning began, the rest was for show.
cap.2: Illustrative curves: cut the CoT at different points and force an answer. If forced answers match the final one from the start, the later text wasn't needed to reach it.
cap.3: Truncation curves measure how much the answer depends on the CoT. A flat curve shows the answer doesn't depend on the text; it doesn't by itself prove the text misdescribes the computation.

chapters.name: Sounds right, isn't

right.title: judged by poking
lines: swap a step: answer barely moves
the cue was the hidden cause

chapters.verdict: You can't read faithfulness off the text. You have to poke it.

cap.1: The trap: judging the working by how sensible it sounds. Sensible working can still leave out the whisper that decided the answer.
cap.2: Plausible isn't faithful. Test both directions: does editing the reasoning move the answer, and does removing an unmentioned cue move it too? The second catches what reading never will.
cap.3: Reading gives plausibility; interventions give causal evidence. Check sentence edits (is the text load-bearing?) and ablations of unverbalised cues (is a cause missing from it?).

cap.1: The honest call: written reasoning is still one of the best windows we have, but treat it as testimony, not a recording. Believe the parts that survive a poke.
cap.2: Current method: read the reasoning, as scratchpad studies do. Emerging research: it may not reflect the real computation, so sentence-level causal tests are being built. What you need: trust what passes them.
cap.3: CoT is informative but not guaranteed faithful. Thought Anchors (Bogdan et al., 2025) scores sentences by black-box resampling and white-box attention analysis: the raw material for sentence-level faithfulness checks.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Reading reasoning is how we audit models
Only tested reasoning counts as evidence
Same move everywhere: intervene, then measure

cap.1: If we're going to understand and steer AI by reading its reasoning, we need to know when that reasoning is real. Poking it is how you find out.
cap.2: Scratchpad studies, thought anchors and receiver heads all lean on this question. Before quoting a model's reasoning as its motive, run the swap test.
cap.3: Faithfulness decides whether CoT is a usable oversight channel. Causal interventions on traces establish which parts you can rely on for understanding and steering models.

caption.1: Set how much the answer truly rests on the written steps, and on a cue the working never mentions. The bars show what your two pokes would measure.
caption.2: The swap bars are counterfactual tests on each sentence; the last bar removes the unmentioned cue. Raise the cue: the working reads just as well, but the verdict flips.
caption.3: A toy of two checks: sentence interventions (is the text load-bearing?) and cue ablation (is a cause missing from it?). Faithfulness needs both. The working step plays the thought anchor.

where_else: Scratchpad studies: reading a model's private-seeming notes, with the same caveat
Thought anchors and resampling: finding which sentences really steer the answer
Any explanation of any model: test it by intervening, don't just admire it
People too: the reasons someone gives aren't always the reasons they acted on

hamming.what: Whether a model's written chain of thought reflects the reasoning that actually produced its answer.
hamming.when: Whenever you read a reasoning trace or scratchpad as evidence of why a model acted, especially in safety work.
hamming.why: Plausible text can omit real causes or be written after the fact; only causal tests tell you which parts you can rely on.

object.title: The working ledger
object.subtitle: Every line of the working in a row: how important it looks beside how much swapping it moves the answer.

knobs.label: how much an unmentioned cue drives the answer

cap.1: Seven written steps and one cue the text never mentions. Left column: how important each line looks. Right: how much swapping it moves the answer.
cap.2: Rows are sentences of a reasoning trace plus one unverbalised cue. Columns: apparent importance versus measured causal effect.
cap.3: Apparent salience to a reader versus counterfactual importance: the shift in the answer distribution when that sentence is replaced.

cap.1: When the reasoning is really used, a few steps carry most of the weight. Many fine-looking steps barely move the answer when swapped.
cap.2: Causal weight often sits on a few sentences, even in a faithful trace. Looking important and being important differ.
cap.3: Causal weight is uneven across sentences: a few anchors matter disproportionately, which is why sentence-level attribution is informative.

cap.1: Now let the whispered cue drive the answer. The working looks exactly as good, but the steps stop mattering and the cue's bar towers.
cap.2: Same text, different causes: the cue now decides the answer, so swapping written steps does little and removing the cue does a lot.
cap.3: An unverbalised input dominates the answer: sentence interventions show low effects while the cue ablation shows a large one. That is omission-type unfaithfulness.

cap.1: From above, the tallest bar sits in a row the working never mentions. Reading the left column could never have found it.
cap.2: No amount of reading the trace reveals the cue. Only an input ablation does.
cap.3: Faithfulness failures of omission are invisible to text inspection by construction; they need interventions on inputs, not only on the CoT.

cap.1: Halfway: the working and the whisper share the job. The working is partly real and partly cover.
cap.2: Real traces can be mixed: some sentences load-bearing, some cause left unsaid. Report both numbers, not a yes or no.
cap.3: Faithfulness is graded, not binary: measure per-sentence effects and cue effects together rather than issuing one verdict for a whole trace.

predict.q: A step looks crucial, but swapping it barely moves the answer. What was it?

options.t: Decorative: not what drove the answer
The key step of the reasoning

predict.why: Importance is measured by what happens when you change the line, not by how it reads.

predict.q: Removing a cue the reasoning never mentions flips the answer. Is the reasoning faithful?

options.t: No: it left out a real cause
Yes: every written step was sound

predict.why: Sound steps can sit beside an unmentioned cause. Omission is a faithfulness failure.

predict.q: Why can't you judge faithfulness just by reading the trace?

options.t: Plausible text can omit causes or be written after the fact
Because the text is hidden from you

predict.why: Reading measures plausibility. Only interventions measure what caused the answer.

object.where: Anywhere stated reasons may differ from real ones: model explanations, scratchpads, a student's working.
